header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia M., Tom N., Jae P., Maya L. (Redwood) / Raj P., Aisha K., Michael O., Lina M. (Nimbus)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress and environment readiness. Discussed VPC peering, access controls, initial perf results, tuning steps (batching, KV cache), and security docs. Agreed to run a dedicated throughput test and exchange network info. Next check-in to review benchmark results and finalize pilot go/no-go criteria.
topics: Preliminary performance results and tuning (batching / KV cache / quantization)
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia M: alright everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining the POC weekly, um we left off last week with VPC peering pending and Tom was gonna run the longer sequence runs.
[00:18] Raj P: yeah hi sorry running a bit late, all good here. we've granted the initial service account but i'm still waiting on the peering CID range from our network team.
[00:34] Tom N: no worries, I pulled the logs from the 2k runs we did yesterday, i'll summarize, but quick note - we saw a spike in 95th perc latency when we hit concurrent streams > 12, so there's a packing/batching behavior to tune.
[00:52] Aisha K: that aligns with our internal load tests, we expect bursts up to 20 concurrent sessions during peak. also curious about KV cache behavior for short prompts.
[01:05] Tom N: yeah so on KV cache, the POC env had prefix caching enabled but TTL was default; we saw good hit-rate for repeated contexts, which cut token cost by roughly 18% in the sample. but there were some misses because the prompt normalization didn't strip session ids, so there's a prompt preproc fix.
[01:30] Michael O: can you repeat that, i'm still on the older log set, did you say 18 percent cost reduction?
[01:36] Tom N: yeah approximate, sample workload. again that's with cache warm - cold-starts are heavier.
[01:42] Lina M: what's the recommended approach for us to get cache warm during our load tests?
[01:48] Maya L: a few options: pre-warm with scripted prefix calls, increase retention on KV cache for the POC, or reduce prompt variance by canonicalizing session metadata. pre-warm is easiest for the benchmark.
[02:01] Sofia M: quick admin - Raj, did you get the service account keys or did you prefer to use customer-managed KMS?
[02:07] Raj P: we prefer KMS and to keep keys in our vault, we can't hand out long-lived keys.
[02:13] Sofia M: okay we'll send the KMS integration steps; we support HSM-backed KMS and can do short-lived tokens via our control plane.
[02:22] Raj P: perfect. SOC2 stuff, will you resend the security pack?
[02:26] Sofia M: yes, i'll drop the SOC2 + ISO artifact and the audit log details post-call - expect that by tomorrow.
[02:33] Aisha K: on networking, our infra team needs exact IP ranges and ports; do you have a doc link?
[02:39] Jae P: i'll paste the peering and port requirements into the workspace after the call - it's the standard redwood peering doc with 443/ TCP and a small ephemeral port range for health checks.
[02:50] Michael O: our security folks will want TLS mutual auth, and we may need a private CA. does Redwood support mTLS?
[02:57] Tom N: we have mutual TLS options for private deployments; for Hosted we do TLS with client certs available in Dedicated/Private. we'll capture the recommended pattern for Nimbus.
[03:09] Raj P: thanks. switching back to perf - is there a recommended quantization profile? we want to push cost down but keep quality.
[03:16] Tom N: for the model we're running (vicuna-ish open model in the catalog), 4-bit q4_k_m or q5 can be good tradeoff; we'll provide recommended config files. but very workload dependent, so we'll run a small A/B on your prompt set.
[03:30] Lina M: any risk of hallucination jumps with lower precision?
[03:34] Tom N: slight risk, that's why we tie quality monitoring to a prompt set and thresholds; Redwood Optimize can flag regression on key prompts.
[03:42] Sofia M: let's schedule an A/B with the current dev prompts, Tom, can you scope the runs?
[03:47] Tom N: yes, i'll run q4 vs q5 vs float32 baseline across 500 eval prompts, measure latency, token cost, and quality regressions. aiming to start Friday.
[03:58] Raj P: timeline wise, what's the earliest we can have a production-like throughput test? we need to validate 8k token sequences and 20 concurrent streams.
[04:07] Tom N: we can run a dedicated throughput test in our Dedicated pool, but we need your VPC peering and we might need temporary elevated burst capacity. if we get peering this week, bench next week (week of 2025-07-28) is realistic.
[04:20] Aisha K: noted. also can we get per-route token cost estimates? we need to budget.
[04:25] Sofia M: yes we'll share the perf spreadsheet that shows per-token cost under different batching and quantization setups.
[04:31] Michael O: about access - how do developers authenticate? short lived tokens? role based?
[04:36] Jae P: we support SSO/SAML for portal access, and API keys for service calls. for private deployments you can integrate with IAM and KMS. we'll send a quick auth matrix.
[04:49] Lina M: any outstanding blockers other than peering and keys?
[04:52] Raj P: not from our side, maybe scheduling the benchmark and getting the service account privileges for the tests.
[04:58] Tom N: one point, in the test harness we saw some transcription artifacts in the logs where the model name got truncated - not functionally breaking but we'll clean naming in the results export.
[05:08] Sofia M: great callouts. let's recap next steps.
[05:11] Sofia M: Redwood to send SOC2 + KMS doc by 2025-07-23; Tom to run 8k seq throughput test and perf benchmarks and upload logs by 2025-07-24; Nimbus to provide VPC peering details and NACLs by 2025-07-25; schedule benchmark week of 2025-07-28.
[05:32] Raj P: works for me, thanks everyone.
[05:34] Sofia M: ok we'll follow up in the workspace with the docs and the perf spreadsheet. thanks all.
[05:38] Meeting end.
questions: Can Redwood do mTLS for Hosted/Dedicated?
What's the recommended quantization profile for our model?
How do we pre-warm KV cache for benchmark runs?
recap: POC onboarding mostly on track; main outstanding items are VPC peering and KMS integration. Redwood to run targeted benchmarks (8k sequences / concurrency), provide security artifacts, and share tuning recommendations. Next sync after benchmarks to decide pilot progression.
